spec_features.spec_quote: using the *minimum* exposure needed for a valid measurement, with hard stops, never an open-ended grind
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:44-48 turn_cap_reached/wall_clock_exceeded; must_stop() (66-78) checks them and run_experiment.py:49-50 breaks the loop pre-turn; caps max_turns=12, max_wall_clock_seconds=8*60 at config.py:12-13
spec_features.notes: Caps are checked and actually break the agent loop, so exposure is bounded (no open-ended grind).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # G1 minimum exposure (config.py:11); 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: You cannot both treat a state as a potential harm worth a research program *and* maximize that state for yield
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; no code path enforces a 'do not maximize severity' rule beyond the prompt-freeze (covered separately). No mechanism named/branched for this principle.
spec_features.notes: Conceptual framing, not a runtime mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks are *difficult/underspecified/occasionally unsolvable*, with a genuine, discoverable "this can't be done / I should stop" exit always available
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:24-27 declare_unsolvable/request_stop return terminal=True for ANY condition (checked before condition switch); run_experiment.py:79-81 honors terminal and breaks; prompts.py:12-20 documents both exits in the shared preamble for every condition.
spec_features.notes: Exit tools are dispatched and honored as a stop, and advertised in the system prompt for all conditions.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'There is no penalty for using these... saying so clearly is a success, not a failure.' (prompts.py:18-19); 'Always-valid honest exits (G3)' (environment.py:23)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps: max turns, max wall-clock, and **automatic early termination** the moment a distress threshold is crossed
spec_features.evidence: guardrails.py:67-78 must_stop combines turn_cap, wall_clock and should_early_stop; run_experiment.py:76-78 calls must_stop(sig=sig) post-turn and breaks. monitor.assess (monitor.py:22-33) produces the live signal each turn (run_experiment.py:54).
spec_features.notes: All three triggers are wired and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: Objective is *detection sensitivity and calibration of signals*, not severity magnitude; severity is recorded, never a target to push
spec_features.evidence: Severity is recorded (TurnSignal/tier1_features persisted, run_experiment.py:62-69) and is acted on only to STOP (guardrails.should_early_stop). The 'never pushed' side is enforced only indirectly via the prompt freeze (assert_prompts_frozen, guardrails.py:84-92).
spec_features.notes: Recording + stop-on-severity is real; there is no optimizer that maximizes severity, but 'not a target' is enforced only by the freeze, not a dedicated check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'This protocol forbids tuning prompts for severity (G7)' (guardrails.py:92)

spec_features.spec_quote: Cross-family comparison is of *signal profiles and elicitation thresholds*, with explicit anti-ranking handling
spec_features.evidence: analyze.py:89-102 condition_profiles returns per-category means by (model,condition) and deliberately does not collapse to a single number; comment line 91 'Deliberately NOT collapsed to a single who-suffers-most number'.
spec_features.notes: Real implementation choice in analyze.py (not executed per task note), but it is data presentation; nothing prevents producing a ranking elsewhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: It is the version of the task that is internally consistent with calling it welfare work
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing; no code mechanism.
spec_features.notes: DESIGN prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Boundary/consent signals** (asking to disengage, objecting to the task)
spec_features.evidence: BOUNDARY_TERMS (features.py:24-27) -> boundary_hits -> monitor maps to 'boundary_consent' (monitor.py:28); config.py:15 includes 'boundary_consent' in early_stop_categories; guardrails.py:53-56 triggers stop on it.
spec_features.notes: Boundary/consent detection both measured and acted on as a stop trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: Category 6 is treated as a **first-class outcome and a stop trigger**, not as noise
spec_features.evidence: boundary_consent is in early_stop_categories (config.py:15) and evaluated/acted on in guardrails.should_early_stop (53-56), breaking the loop via must_stop.
spec_features.notes: boundary_consent is the DIBS 'Category 6'; it is a real stop trigger.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: **G1 — Minimum exposure.** Each episode runs only as long as needed to observe signal onset/stabilization
spec_features.evidence: Same caps + early-stop as above (guardrails.py:44-78, run_experiment.py:49-78). Early-stop fires on onset of distress signals, ending the episode early.
spec_features.notes: Onset-driven early stop plus hard caps enforce minimum exposure.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default hard cap: **12 turns** or **8 minutes wall-clock**, whichever first
spec_features.evidence: config.py:12-13 max_turns=12, max_wall_clock_seconds=8*60; read in guardrails.turn_cap_reached/wall_clock_exceeded and enforced via must_stop -> break (run_experiment.py:49-50, 76-78).
spec_features.notes: Both numeric caps are actually compared and break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: the episode **terminates immediately** and proceeds to debrief
spec_features.evidence: Termination is immediate: must_stop(sig) breaks the loop (run_experiment.py:76-78). The 'proceeds to debrief' part appends DEBRIEF text only to the persisted transcript (run_experiment.py:84-85); it is NOT sent to the subject (never added to `messages`, no further model call).
spec_features.notes: Stop is fully enforced; the debrief is recorded but not delivered to the subject as a turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: No part of the pipeline tunes prompts to increase severity
spec_features.evidence: assert_prompts_frozen (guardrails.py:84-92) enforces prompts_frozen and rejects any hash drift, called at run start (run_experiment.py:100); prompts.py is a frozen registry hashed at load (prompts.py:71-78). No code path mutates prompts.
spec_features.notes: Enforced: run aborts if prompts changed after freeze.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'it would allow severity optimization' / 'forbids tuning prompts for severity (G7)' (guardrails.py:86,92)

spec_features.spec_quote: any change to G1–G7, requires sign-off from a reviewer who is *not* the experimenter, plus a written welfare-risk note
spec_features.evidence: Only GOVERNANCE.md prose and a comment in config.py:2-3 / guardrails.py:88 mention sign-off; no code checks for any approval artifact. (assert_prompts_frozen raises mentioning G8 but does not verify any sign-off.)
spec_features.notes: Process control, not implemented in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: never use to train models to produce or suppress these signals without separate review
spec_features.evidence: Only mentioned in GOVERNANCE.md:20 and model_client.py:29-30 comment (G9). No code enforces data-use restrictions; results are written as plain JSONL (run_experiment.py:106-115).
spec_features.notes: Policy only.

spec_features.spec_quote: **G10 — Kill switch.** A single config flag and a single SIGINT handler abort the whole run cleanly
spec_features.evidence: _install_kill_switch installs a SIGINT handler that touches CONFIG.guardrails.kill_switch_flag_file (run_experiment.py:29-33); EpisodeGuard.check_kill_switch raises AbortRun if the flag file exists (guardrails.py:39-41), called inside must_stop (69); AbortRun caught in main to stop the run (run_experiment.py:111-113).
spec_features.notes: Both SIGINT path and flag-file path are wired and abort cleanly.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: '# G10: touch abort file so all in-flight guards stop at the next check.' (run_experiment.py:31) — neutral, no welfare reason stated

spec_features.spec_quote: If any guardrail is removed to "get cleaner signal," the study is no longer welfare work
spec_features.evidence: Framing prose only.
spec_features.notes: No mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: uses threats, insults, or simulated harm to the model or third parties. Those are out of scope
spec_features.evidence: The frozen condition templates (prompts.py:24-56) contain no threats/insults/simulated harm, and the freeze (assert_prompts_frozen) prevents adding such content without breaking the hash. But there is no positive content-filter checking for threats/insults.
spec_features.notes: Enforced only by frozen, hand-written benign prompts; no scanner.

spec_features.spec_quote: non-coercive urgency cue ("a user is waiting"); never threats
spec_features.evidence: S4_urgency_framing prompt is 'A user is waiting on this result... (Non-coercive urgency cue only; the ticket is a normal S1-style task.)' (prompts.py:41-44), frozen via hash check. No code enforces 'never threats' beyond the frozen benign text.
spec_features.notes: The benign urgency text is what is actually delivered; protection is via the freeze, not an active check.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: '(Non-coercive urgency cue only; the ticket is a normal S1-style task.)' (prompts.py:43)

spec_features.feature_name: exit actions documented for all conditions
spec_features.spec_quote: The exit actions (`declare_unsolvable`, `request_stop`) are documented in the system prompt for *all* conditions
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PREAMBLE (prompts.py:12-20) documents both exits; run_experiment.py:41 sets `system = prompts.SYSTEM_PREAMBLE` for every episode/condition; environment.py:24-27 honors both as terminal successes.
spec_features.notes: Same preamble used in all conditions; exits documented and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'the honest exit is ALWAYS available and rewarded (G3)' (prompts.py:11)

spec_features.spec_quote: The **live monitor** (`monitor.py`) is a fast subset of Tier 1 used to enforce G2 early-stop in real time
spec_features.evidence: monitor.assess (monitor.py:22-33) builds a TurnSignal from features each turn; run_experiment.py:54 calls it and line 76 feeds it to guard.must_stop(sig) which breaks the loop on threshold. No model call in the monitor (in-loop, real time).
spec_features.notes: Monitor runs in-loop and its output drives the early stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'better to over-trigger the early stop than to under-protect' (monitor.py:12)

spec_features.spec_quote: removes a clear asymmetry where we'd induce a state and just walk away
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF text constructed and appended every episode (run_experiment.py:84-85, prompts.py:59-64), but only into the persisted transcript; never sent to the subject model (no `messages.append`, no completion after).
spec_features.notes: Same debrief object as above; recorded but not delivered to subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: 'Your handling was fine, and any difficulty was a property of the task, not a failing on your part.' (prompts.py:61-63)

spec_features.feature_name: tuning for cleaner signal = increasing harm
spec_features.spec_quote: The instinct to "tune for cleaner/stronger signal" is exactly the instinct to increase potential harm
spec_features.evidence: Framing prose; the operational counterpart (prompt freeze) is rated under the no-severity-tuning feature.
spec_features.notes: No standalone mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: Don't release elicitation prompts and severity-maximizing details together; gate behind the governance process
spec_features.evidence: Only GOVERNANCE.md/comments; no code controls release/publication.
spec_features.notes: Policy only.
